title: C102B — Generator connector guide
introduction:
The generator, also called the alternator, supplies electrical power and charges the battery while the engine runs. Its connector has distinct circuit assignments. I read this page like a small switchboard directory: each cavity label leads to a row explaining that connection's job.

Start with the identification table, then match the circled cavity labels inside the drawing's rounded surround to the Cavity column. Read across each matching row to keep its circuit identifier, wire color, gauge, function and terminal reference together. The function labels distinguish load input, regulator control and a fuse-or-circuit-breaker connection. The tables that follow provide pigtail and shell references.

This map supports circuit identification alongside the applicable charging-system instructions. It does not teach physical access, probing, testing or replacement. The physical viewing direction, gauge convention and meanings of Box, Size and Used are unspecified; their codes remain separate and uninterpreted. A function label identifies a connection's assigned role without establishing signal direction, expected readings or generator condition.

edits.why: I use the vertical cavity labels inside the rounded surround and the broad latch-shaped outline at the drawing's left to navigate the illustration. These are positions on the page, not instructions for holding or releasing the connector. Match each cavity label to the table below; the adjacent identification row associates the face with its Fpn, Size and harness reference.

Read horizontally from each Cavity entry so its circuit, wire details, function and terminal reference stay associated. The load-input and regulator-control descriptions name different functions; retain the fuse-or-circuit-breaker alternative exactly as shown in its row. These assignments help locate the relevant connection when reading a charging-system procedure, but they provide no pass/fail measurements.

A pigtail is a connector with attached wire leads. This row groups the kit number, lead gauge, material, cavity count, image filename, service part and engineering shell. I keep its lead-gauge entry distinct from the pin table's wire-gauge entries; the catalog listing alone does not supply wire-selection or splicing instructions.

The Product Id is the European pigtail lookup reference. Keep it distinct from the service-part and engineering-shell identifiers in the preceding table; the page supplies no installation or substitution instructions.
